name: LAOS

flag.title: Flag of Laos
flag.note: Red, blue, red — white disc for unity

lead: Laos is a forested country in Southeast Asia. It is the only one in the region with no coast. The Mekong River flows along its western edge past rice paddies and temple towns.

facts.label: Area
facts.sub: A bit bigger than the UK

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Nearly three-quarters of Laos is steep mountain and thick jungle. The cool Bolaven Plateau (high flat land) is famous for coffee and waterfalls.
The Mekong runs 1,835 km along the western border. In the south, Si Phan Don means 'Four Thousand Islands'.
animals: Around 700 Asian elephants still roam the forests of Laos. Moon bears, clouded leopards and the unicorn-like saola (a rare horned animal) hide in the Annamite mountains.
The Mekong once held sacred Irrawaddy dolphins. The last one in Laos died in 2022. Giant Mekong catfish, up to 300 kg, still lurk in deep pools.
culture: Lao meals are shared, with sticky rice, fish, herbs and papaya salad called som tam.
Buddhism shapes daily life. At sunrise in Luang Prabang, hundreds of monks in saffron (orange) robes walk silently through the streets. They collect rice.
history: The kingdom of Lan Xang, 'Million Elephants', began in 1353. It once stretched from China's Yunnan border to Cambodia. Luang Prabang was its golden capital.

France made Laos a colony (a land it ruled) in 1893. Laos gained independence in 1953. Between 1964 and 1973, during the Vietnam War, the US secretly dropped over two million tonnes of bombs. A third never exploded and still hurts people.
wows: Laos is Southeast Asia's only landlocked country, with not one centimetre of coastline.
Laos is the most bombed country per person in history.
Thousands of stone jars on the Plain of Jars weigh up to 14 tonnes. They are over 2,500 years old.
Laotians eat an average of 171 kg of sticky rice each year, a world record.
The saola, an animal found in 1992, is so rare. No scientist has seen one alive in the wild.
Landlocked Laos has Si Phan Don, 'Four Thousand Islands', more islands than many countries with a coast.
Pha That Luang, a temple in the capital Vientiane, is covered in real gold.

myths.myth: Laos is always hot and tropical
myths.fact: Highland towns like Phonsavan drop near freezing in winter.
Elephants suck water up into the trunk. Then they squirt it into their mouths.
